authType.description: Legacy authentication type field. Older provisioning stored the auth type here; the backend copies its value into `authenticationType` on load. Prefer `authenticationType` for new configurations.

authenticationType.description: How Grafana authenticates to the Google Sheets and Google Drive APIs. `jwt` uses a Google JWT service account key file; `key` uses an API key and only works with public spreadsheets; `gce` uses the GCE default service account.

clientEmail.description: Service account email from the JWT key file (the `client_email` field).

defaultProject.description: Google Cloud project ID that owns the enabled Sheets and Drive APIs.

defaultSheetID.description: Optional spreadsheet ID to use as default when creating new queries

privateKeyPath.description: Path on the Grafana server to a file containing the JWT private key. Use this instead of pasting the private key inline.

tokenUri.description: OAuth 2.0 token endpoint from the JWT key file (the `token_uri` field, typically `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`).

secureValues.description: JWT private key (the `private_key` field of the service account key file). Supply this or `privateKeyPath`, not both.

Legacy write-only secret used by older versions of the plugin. The backend still checks this first and, if set, uses it in place of `privateKey`/`clientEmail`/`tokenUri`; new configurations should use `privateKey` instead. If you are migrating away from this field, you must also clear it, otherwise the old credentials remain active.

gce.description: Credentials are retrieved from the GCE metadata server. Requires Grafana to be running on a Google Compute Engine virtual machine. No secrets are stored.

jwt.description: Service account credentials. Reads private and public spreadsheets. Set secure.privateKey.create to the `private_key` value from the service account JSON, or set spec.jsonData.privateKeyPath to a file on the Grafana server instead.

key.description: Simplest configuration, but only reads spreadsheets that are shared publicly.
